newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia PM says Israel reneging on peace deal.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia PM says Israel reneging on peace deal.

text.p: Malaysia believes the new Israeli government is trying to renege on a 1993 peace deal between Israel and the Palestinians, local newspapers on Sunday quoted Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad as saying.

"We feel the (Israeli) government is trying to unmake an agreement that was made freely between two parties. If successor governments forget or renege on promises made by previous governments, then there will be no security for anyone," newspapers quoted Mahathir as saying.
He was speaking to accompanying Malaysian media in New York after addressing the United Nations General Assembly.
"Whether you like an agreement or not you have to work within the premises of the agreement," he said.
He said multicultural but predominantly Moslem Malaysia will not consider recognising the state of Israel until the country met its obligations under the 1993 peace accord with the Palestinians.
"We have always felt that we will not recognise them until they have fulfilled all the undertakings under the agreement," Mahathir was quoted as saying.
He also blasted the western media for giving an impression it was the Palestinians who were the cause of the violence.

The daily New Straits Times said Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi criticised Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government at a United Nations Security Council meeting for placing "new obstacles to the peace process".
He said Israel's decision to open up a tunnel near the Al-Aqsa mosque was an act of provocation.
"We condemn this blatant act of provocation by Israel and call on Israel to respect the sanctity of the Al-Aqsa most and Al-Haram Al Sharif and to close the tunnel," he said.
